\chapter{What the evidence changes about the proposed service}
\label{rewrite:evidence-consequences}

The four journeys distinguish a wrong target, insufficient treatment support,
causal ambiguity and uncertain measurement. Those failures demand different
responses. A common service should make the distinctions visible while
reusing the appropriate statistical procedures. Its initial scope follows
from the evidence below; it does not require every possible capability to
be implemented at once.

\section{A result should change a design choice}
The existing 3,000-replication generated offer study is evidence about target
alignment. Under one specified design, the residual projection averages
26.447 when the equal-population benefit is 50. Its interval covers its own
target in 97.2\% of repetitions and the population target in none. At the
stipulated cost of 40, interpreting it as the population effect rejects the
beneficial offer in all 500 repetitions of that scenario. The design
consequence is to put the population weights and target in the result,
and to compare implementations only after aligning those quantities. A
more precise projection is not a repair for this interpretation error.

The separate 6,000-replication sparse-support study addresses inference
after the target is aligned. Pooling yields 94.7\% conditional coverage
under equal normal variances but 52.2\% under the tested unequal-variance
case. Cellwise Student intervals joined by a union bound preserve the
conditional coverage guarantee in the normal model at the cost of very
wide intervals. Thus the initial implementation should show cell support
and retain an unsupported or inconclusive result. If useful precision
requires unjustified pooling, the next expenditure should improve assignment
support or the information collected. These are existing generated
experiments, not evidence of superiority by a named external package.

The public UCI timing study answers a different question. On 41,188 archived
contact records, later-archive prediction has AUC 0.630 using the candidate
pre-call feature set and 0.793 when duration is added. The latter feature
is unavailable before the call, so its predictive gain cannot justify
pre-call targeting. Differences between early and late archive outcomes
also matter for evaluation. The correct service response is to preserve
availability dates and the evaluation period. Neither score estimates
the effect of making a call. Chapter~\ref{scisyn:evidence} gives the
executed design, comparators, results and qualifications.

The retained public 401(k), monetary, panel and linked-record analyses
provide further empirical and methodological context. Their sampling,
instrument, design and observation restrictions remain attached to their
results in the detailed evidence part. A working independent-observation
covariance in a public application does not validate a bank's common-calendar
uncertainty. A successful finite construction does not settle the unrestricted
linked-history problem. The negative findings remain relevant because
they identify the information a future bank study must supply.

The new one-sample deposit calculation in Chapter~\ref{rewrite:deposit}
completes the numerical route from estimation to contribution. Its callable
and command-line agreement tests the delivery of that particular report.
The four existing library/CLI/MCP cases test semantic consistency for
their own operations, including unsupported dependence. They establish
complementary facts. Neither is a matched analyst trial, a full general
estimation service, or evidence of improved bank outcomes.

\section{Choose the smallest comparison that can reverse the recommendation}
The first comparison should take the same fixed offer question through
expert composition and a minimal shared integration. The cases should
include correct assignment, heterogeneous effects, unequal treatment
support, unavailable predictors, misrecorded receipt and a dependent
sampling request outside the accepted route. The generated law supplies
truth where that is possible; a public case supplies realistic data handling
without pretending its causal truth is known. A valid refusal counts as
a completed scientific answer when the information is insufficient.

An independent evaluator should judge target correctness, assumption
visibility, uncertainty, interpretation and avoidable errors. Time must
include correction, interpretation and unsuccessful attempts. The estimate
itself is not a success metric when its target differs from the request.
The proposed comparison is not yet an executed analyst study; its purpose
is to discover whether the common representation is worth its expense.
If both workflows reach equivalent answers at equivalent cost, improve
the existing workflow. If the integration reduces consequential errors or
repeated work, a narrow bank-data pilot becomes a defensible next step.

\chapter{Which tasks merit language assistance?}
\label{rewrite:assistance-tasks}

Assistance should be selected by the task it improves. A system that answers
questions about a supplied causal mechanism has not thereby shown that
it can discover a defensible mechanism for a new bank. The evidence
synthesis in Chapter~\ref{scisyn:assistance} and the detailed studies
support a restricted comparison, with a questionnaire and ordinary search
as serious alternatives. They do not establish a measured saving for this
proposed product.

\section{Formulation and variable construction}
For formulation, the useful output is a precise intervention, alternative,
population, outcome, horizon and information date, together with unresolved
choices. The retained Kıcıman and causal-learn+ discussions motivate
question clarification and graph critique. Their descriptions support
a prototype candidate, not the truth of bank-specific assumptions.
\citep{v12_la_2305_00050,v12_la_2606_23608}
The strongest elementary comparator is a structured questionnaire completed
by an economist. Measure material omissions found and the time required
to correct the final question. The deposit distinction among assignment,
receipt, acceptance and price is an explicit test case. An eloquent
answer that silently chooses one is a failure.

Variable construction requires a separate assessment. A model can suggest
a record field or an extraction rule, but measurement validity depends
on the relation between that field and the scientific variable. The
retained text-and-causal-inference review discusses text used for adjustment;
it does not prove that a modern embedding removes confounding.
\citep{exec13_census_text_review_arxiv}
Compare any proposed extraction with a documented coding rule and
independently labelled examples, preserving missing and ambiguous cases.
The observation journey shows why high predictive accuracy or apparent
completeness is insufficient. Begin with auditable field definitions and
retrieval assistance; an autonomous scientific measurement claim remains
unsupported without independent validation.

\section{Diagrams and numerical discovery}
For diagram work, require evidence and timing for each proposed relationship
and retain competing explanations. LACR's reported retrieval effects vary
across its examples. The retained inspection records both improvement and
deterioration, including the ASIA skeleton comparison and the SACHS
comparison when PC output is added. This is evidence for evaluating the
retrieval choice, rather than assuming that more context improves the graph.
\citep{v12_la_2402_15301}
Compare the assistant with ordinary search plus an economist and, where
its assumptions fit, a numerical discovery procedure. The inputs must
be matched. Assess false orientations, missed common causes and the
resulting effect or action, rather than relying solely on edge counts.

The first assistant should propose a diagram and competing explanations
for review, then call a named discovery or identification method under
explicit assumptions. Numerical discovery contributes its own evidence;
textual plausibility cannot turn an unresolved equivalence class into
a validated graph. The three-model pricing example is a useful adverse
case because one unjustified orientation changes the financial sign.

\section{A positive workflow result and its limits}
The retained ORCA study gives a more direct reason to test assistance in a
completed workflow. Twelve participants used a counterbalanced within-subjects
design; the baseline assistant already had tools, step gates and minimal
state. The paper's Figure 5 reports total task durations of 1,395 seconds
for the baseline and 1,107 seconds for ORCA, a reported reduction of about
21\%. Table 1 reports completion rates 0.75 and 0.83. This is positive
published evidence for a structured workflow on the study's relational,
generated causal tasks. It is not a measured benefit for this banking
proposal. \citep[pp.~3--5]{exec13_census_orca}

The interpretation changes when the outcome definitions and all attempted
analyses are retained. Completion means producing an ATE, regardless of
accuracy; discovery success requires the treatment and outcome nodes to be
present. The paper's confidence-interval metric is described as an estimated
ATE falling within a ground-truth interval, so its reported 0.083 and 0.50
must not be presented as conventional repeated-sample confidence coverage.
The full-data condition comparison for absolute ATE error has $p=0.321$;
after excluding configuration-error outliers, the reported OLS comparison
has $p=0.020$. Both belong in an assessment of completed work because
configuration errors are among the failures a service is supposed to avoid.
The abstract's claimed 42-percentage-point completion gain also differs
from the displayed 0.75-to-0.83 comparison; this synthesis uses the stated
table comparison rather than reconciling that discrepancy by invention.
\citep[pp.~1, 5, 17--18]{exec13_census_orca}

The proposal should therefore test whether shared intermediate results and
question clarification save full effort while preserving scientific quality.
It should retain all configuration failures and report separately the time
spent by the analyst, tool execution and correction. The external study
supports that experiment's plausibility. Its small participant sample,
specified tasks, outcome definitions and analysis exclusions prevent a
claim that the same benefit is established across bank studies.

\section{Identification, execution and reporting}
CLadder evaluates formal causal questions under constructed mechanisms;
its reported results concern historical models and that supplied task.
It does not measure elicitation of a new bank mechanism.
\citep{v12_la_2312_04350}
For identification, compare assistance with a defined formal procedure,
requiring the assistant to preserve both the answer and its conditions.
An appropriate refusal must explain the missing restriction, not simply
return an empty result. The benchmark literature and the retained
mechanism-clustering critiques give reasons to keep failed cases and
uncertainty denominators in the evaluation.

For execution, the existing local interface study shows equality for four
constructed requests, not model-driven analysis quality. A scripted
workflow is the credible baseline. Compare any assistant on request
construction, faithful tool use, errors detected and correction effort.
Do not give it credit for a calculation performed by the formal tool
while omitting the costs of choosing or correcting the request.

For reporting, a deterministic template is a strong comparator because
it can already state the estimand, assumptions, interval and scope.
The assistant's proposed value is explaining why the result changes a
decision or why it cannot yet support one. Check that explanation
against the actual result and the retained sources. A report that turns
a set crossing zero into a positive recommendation fails even if its
prose is persuasive. No local live-model evaluation establishes an
incremental benefit for this reporting task.

The preferred first assisted task is therefore question clarification
with evidence retrieval and explicit alternatives, evaluated against
the questionnaire. Identification and numerical results remain delegated
to defined procedures. Expansion to autonomous discovery, variable
construction or recommendations requires task-specific evidence. The
frontier census remains 82 inspected and 31 unread; this synthesis does
not claim those omissions have been resolved. A live comparison still
requires a fixed model version, held-out questions, matched information,
independent adjudication and a budget.

\chapter{The first investment and the evidence that would reverse it}
\label{rewrite:investment-decision}

The immediate proposal is a minimal comparative integration for a fixed
offer study, with explicit population weights, information dates and
a complete financial report. Reuse a transparent estimator and retain
a documented alternative. The seventeen-area comparison establishes
which further capabilities are plausible candidates and why they need
separate assumptions. It is not a reason to build all seventeen before
evaluating the first study.

\section{Compare equivalent completed studies}
There are four economically serious alternatives. Expert composition
uses existing methods and bespoke study documentation. Minimal integration
adds a reusable request and result description around selected methods.
A broad shared service adds more methods, languages, maintenance and
operating commitments. A commercial route can provide supported
procedures and existing institutional integration, but its relevant
entitlements, actual prices and matched capabilities are unknown here.
The detailed commercial discussions preserve documented features and
unknowns; an unobserved feature is not evidence that it is absent.

The proposed first comparison selects minimal integration against expert
composition. Its potential gains come from repeated target specification,
information-date checks, error detection and reporting. Fitting a regression
may occupy little of the total work. Any proposed saving must therefore
be measured over preparation, correction, interpretation and failed
attempts. Bespoke causal reasoning remains part of every alternative.

Let $N$ be annual studies genuinely eligible for this restricted route;
$h$ hours saved per completed study at equivalent quality; $w$ loaded
hourly cost; $D$ reduction in expected decision loss per study; $C$ annual
operating cost; and $K$ annualised development and adoption cost. Then
\[
 B=N(wh+D)-C-K.
\]
The conditional break-even study volume is $(C+K)/(wh+D)$ only when
$wh+D>0$. A negative denominator cannot be repaired by doing more studies.
The earlier illustrative investment account in Chapter~\ref{r3:investment}
retains its actual stipulated inputs and arithmetic, including the
26.74-study threshold. That threshold belongs to that account. It must
not be imported as an observed requirement for the newly selected scope.

The deposit example's \pounds3 population contribution concerns one
constructed customer action. It is not $D$, the improvement in decision
loss due to choosing one analytical workflow over another. Counting
that whole contribution as a software benefit would confuse policy value
with the incremental value of analysis. Similarly, correction hours
counted in $h$ must not be counted again in $D$. These distinctions
prevent an attractive worked example from becoming an invented ROI.

\section{A spending sequence with real alternatives}
The first expenditure buys a matched analyst comparison using the
constructed and public cases, with independently assessed scientific
quality and recorded full effort. It asks whether the small integration
changes decisions or reduces work enough to pay for its ongoing cost.
A bank-data pilot follows only if that evidence is favourable and the
bank supplies a defensible target, data access, assignment information
and a meaningful precision requirement. An operating trial then tests
the relevant interfaces and platform under its actual conditions.

Several observations would reverse or narrow the recommendation. Equal
quality and effort favour the established workflow. A commercial
entitlement supplying equivalent outputs at lower full cost favours
that route. Frequent lack of treatment support or reliable observation
truth favours better study design and data collection. A repeated
need for unsupported dependent inference limits the offer route rather
than justifying a broad claim. Evidence of consequential, reproducibly
avoided errors or lower full effort can justify extending the integration.

This is a conditional proposal with a selected next experiment. It
preserves the larger scientific and software programme without treating
its unfinished questions as already solved. The detailed comparisons
and operating evidence that follow allow a reader to inspect those
restrictions and alternatives before funding the next step.

\section{Buy a method for a question}

The software comparisons support selective reuse. A bank should first specify
the comparison it needs, then choose an estimator or discovery method whose
assumptions fit. The programming language affects maintenance and practical
use; it does not determine whether an effect is identified. Commercial support
may be worth paying for, but a licence cannot resolve an ambiguity in the
economic model. The comparisons of commercial identification, panel methods
and longitudinal inference develop this distinction in detail.

For a deposit offer, the choice begins with the population and intervention.
If the bank asks for an average effect across eligible households, an estimator
that weights households by variation in treatment answers the same question
only under additional conditions. The EconML comparison derives this issue:
a constant residual projection weights conditional effects by
$e(S)\{1-e(S)\}$, where $e(S)$ is the probability of receiving treatment in
stratum $S$. That can differ from the population average when effects vary.
This is a reason to specify and check the target, rather than to reject a
flexible estimator as a class.~\citep{exec19_econml_source,exec19_econml_reference}

\label{gap29:software-followup}
The public experiment demonstrates why reuse is the starting point. Native
R fitting and a separate Python calculation agree on the same observations,
regression specification and HC2 covariance. Rewriting a familiar estimator
in another language would add little to that calculation. The proposal's
contribution must instead be demonstrated in the connection between the
economic question, assumptions, available information and reported decision.

\section{Panel estimation is already a commercial capability}
The official MATLAB documentation retrieved on 29 October 2026 describes
one-way fixed- and random-effects panel regressions. The fixed-effects
documentation explains transformed-data estimation, a subject-clustered
sandwich option and handling of missing measurements. It documents
\texttt{fitfepanel} as introduced in R2026b and
\texttt{fitrepanel} in R2026a. The retrieved pages are current R2026b pages;
their exact availability before the 7 October literature cutoff has not been
established. They are a dated capability update, not a reconstructed
pre-cutoff software comparison. \citep{gap29matlab}

The documented treatment of missing identifiers is consequential: a record
with an absent subject identifier is assigned an additional group, while a
missing predictor or response removes the observation from estimation.
Those are computational conventions, not evidence that the economic unit
is known or that discarded observations are ignorable. The panel study in
Chapter~\ref{gap29:funding} shows why that distinction matters.

A matched comparison must specify the institution and time effects,
covariance convention, initial sample and missing-record treatment before
comparing coefficients. The inspected pages describe a one-way model and
subject clustering; they are not sufficient evidence about every possible
way to obtain time effects or two-way covariance in the wider MATLAB estate.
There has been no licensed MATLAB execution in this study. The appropriate
proposal decision is to retain it as an existing-estate alternative and
test the declared calculation where the institution already has access.
Claims of missing commercial capability would require broader evidence.

\section{A decision diagram already contains an information structure}
HUGIN's official GUI 9.8 manual describes Bayesian networks, decision and
utility nodes, and limited-memory influence diagrams. Its account makes
the information available at each decision explicit through incoming
informational links; it also relaxes the traditional requirement that every
earlier observation remains available. This is directly relevant to a
servicing policy, where later actions must use the information actually
observed at their dates. \citep{gap29hugin}

The proposal should therefore compare a graph assistant with an established
diagram editor and a declared decision model. It should not equate drawing
an arrow with identifying an intervention effect, or infer from a manual
that the proposed integration has been implemented. The inspected material
supports a concrete alternative for representing decisions and information;
it does not establish an automatic solution to latent confounding or missing
outcomes.

The vendor's published licence text makes distribution using its API subject
to an OEM licence. That term changes the proposed reuse route: an internal
connection to an entitled installation and redistribution of a new product
are different propositions. The actual order, deployment conditions and
prices remain to be established with the vendor. The current manual's exact
release date relative to the literature cutoff is also unresolved.
\citep{gap29huginlicense}

\section{Which comparisons belong before a prototype}
The proposal can justify selecting existing estimators and diagram tools
from inspected methods, alternatives and explicit limitations. A complete
installed distribution, matched adverse-data tests and target-system
acceptance are subsequent implementation evidence. They must be specified
before a native adapter is accepted, but they should not be treated as
proof that the economic case for a prototype is unfinished in every respect.

DoubleML, \texttt{did}, \texttt{causaleffect}, and the named commercial
causaLens offering still require their previously identified version,
method or reuse questions to be resolved where those questions could change
the selection. The present calculations neither execute those packages
nor certify their adapters. The commercial source follow-up narrows two
documentation gaps; it does not complete the 102-cell software census.
The decision remains to compare a narrow integration with the institution's
existing practice, and to spend on implementation only where that comparison
can reveal a material analytical benefit.

\chapter{Using assistance where its value can be tested}
\label{scisyn:assistance}

\section{From a business request to a study}
A request to improve retention is not yet an intervention. An economist needs
to distinguish an invitation, acceptance of an offer, a price change and a
repeated contact policy; specify who is eligible; and choose the outcome and
information date. The retained language-model literature motivates assistance
with such formulation and graph critique, while retaining the role of formal
analysis. Its demonstrations do not establish bank-specific assumptions.
\citep{v12_la_2305_00050,v12_la_2606_23608}

The first prototype should produce competing questions when the request is
ambiguous. For example, the effect of offering a fee waiver among all eligible
customers differs from the effect among customers who accept it. Acceptance
can depend on unobserved intentions. A structured questionnaire is a strong
baseline: if it obtains the same defensible question more cheaply, it should
be preferred. Assistance earns its cost when it discovers a material omission,
finds relevant evidence or reduces correction time.

\section{A diagram is an argument about mechanisms}
Require each proposed edge to state its economic interpretation, timing and
evidence. An assistant can suggest competing explanations and retrieve primary
sources. It should retain uncertainty when the sources disagree or do not
describe the bank's process. The LACR paper reports both improved and worsened
retrieval-assisted graph results across its examples. This supports a comparison
of retrieval choices, not a blanket claim that more retrieved text improves
discovery.
\citep{v12_la_2402_15301}

Evaluate diagram assistance against three alternatives: an unaided economist,
a questionnaire plus ordinary search, and numerical discovery under declared
assumptions. Match the permitted information. Count unsupported orientations,
missed common causes and changes in the resulting intervention conclusions.
Edge accuracy alone can obscure a serious error if one wrong edge changes
whether an action is beneficial. Conversely, an unresolved graph can be useful
when all credible members support the same decision.

\section{Formal reasoning, tools and honest refusal}
CLadder studies formal causal questions under constructed mechanisms. Its
reported historical benchmark results are evidence about that task, not a
measure of how well an assistant elicits a causal model from an unfamiliar
bank. The causal-learn+ discussion separately describes assistance around data
inspection, assumptions, algorithms and interpretation.
\citep{v12_la_2312_04350,v12_la_2606_23608}

For identification, the assistant should call a defined method and preserve
the method's conclusion and scope. For estimation, it should retain the target,
sample, observation dates and uncertainty. For reporting, it should explain
which conclusions depend on which assumptions. For a repeated policy, it must
preserve information available at each action rather than treat all later
measurements as adjustment variables. A failed or unsupported calculation
should prompt a revised question or an explanation of the missing information.

There is no live language-model evaluation in this new evidence. A defensible
next comparison needs a fixed model and version, permitted inputs, held-out
questions, human adjudication independent of the tested system and a budget.
The evaluation should include correction time and the financial importance of
errors as well as answer accuracy. Missing those inputs limits a claim of
measured benefit; it does not prevent developing the scientific comparison or
using a simple baseline now.

\section{Improve the question before automating the answer}

The strongest proposal for language assistance begins with tasks that a bank
economist can inspect: separating an invitation from actual participation,
identifying which information was available before a decision, proposing
alternative causal diagrams, and finding the source of an assumption. These

a conventional search, or an unaided analyst.~\citep{v12_la_2305_00050,v12_la_2606_23608}

does not establish what happened in a bank. A process record showing that an
invitation was randomized has a different evidential role from a model's

when the retrieved material is relevant and reliable. The reported LACR
comparisons include adverse as well as favourable retrieval outcomes, which
makes indiscriminate retrieval an inadequate design recommendation.

\section{Keep the economist's judgment visible}

The literature distinguishes answering questions about a supplied causal
structure from discovering the right structure for a new problem. CLadder
tests formal causal questions under constructed mechanisms. Causal-learn+
concerns assistance with numerical causal analysis. Evidence from either

sampling design as the numerical method. For reporting, ask whether the
reader can distinguish a conditional estimate from an unsupported causal
assertion. The relevant cost includes analyst correction and unresolved cases,
as well as model calls. These are proposed comparisons; the reviewed literature
does not supply a general estimate of savings for this bank.

than credible alternatives. A study in which a simple questionnaire performs
as well would support using the questionnaire. A method that gives fluent
answers while changing the causal question should be rejected for that use.

\chapter{When repeated readings add information}
\label{gap29:measurement}

A bank may ask an assistant to recover financial distress from customer
notes before assessing the effect of a servicing action. Reading the same
notes several times is attractive because disagreement is easy to observe.
Agreement can be less informative: several readers may share the same
omission. The distinction affects whether text can help control confounding.
The literature on text-based causal adjustment identifies measurement error,
collider information and post-treatment content as separate problems.
\citep{exec13_census_text_review_arxiv}

\section{A common error creates a lower limit}
Consider a project model, not an empirical claim about any language model.
Let latent distress be $U$, the action index $A=U+\varepsilon_A$, and
the outcome $Y=\tau A+U+\varepsilon_Y$, with $\tau=-1/5$. The latent
variable and the two disturbances are independent, centred, unit-variance
Gaussians. Suppose reading $j$ produces $W_j=U+e_j$. The measurement errors
are independent of $U,\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_Y$, have variance $s$ and
equal pairwise correlation $\rho$. These premises make the calculation
transparent; actual extraction errors may violate all of them.

The averaged reading has error variance
\[
 s_m=\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=1}^m e_j\right)
     =s\left(\rho+\frac{1-\rho}{m}\right).
\]
The covariance of $(A,\overline W)$ is
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&1\\1&1+s_m\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
and its covariance with $Y$ is $(2\tau+1,\tau+1)'$. Solving these two
normal equations gives the coefficient on $A$ after adjustment:
\[
 \beta_{A\mid\overline W}=\tau+\frac{s_m}{1+2s_m}.
\]

\chapter{What a causal reasoning test measures}
\label{gap29:frontier}
A banking analyst asks several different questions of an assistant. Can it
translate a request for higher deposits into an intervention and a measurable
target? Can it distinguish information known before an offer from information
created by the offer? Can it explain which arrows in a diagram are assumptions,
and recognise when several diagrams fit the same observations? A correct
answer to a narrative puzzle is useful evidence about some of these abilities,
but it does not establish all of them.

\section{Explanations deserve their own test}
Wang and Shen examine three constructed scenarios: coin operations, interrupted
file downloads and a hypothetical vaccination calculation. Four variants of
each scenario and three prompting approaches give 36 prompt conditions.
Their scoring distinguishes a correct result and explanation, a flawed
explanation, and an incorrect result. This is valuable because a correct
number can accompany a mistaken economic argument. The study reports mixed
changes from examples and guided reasoning, rather than a uniformly helpful
prompting intervention. \citep{gap29wangshen}

The terms used in a benchmark also need scrutiny. The paper calls reasoning
from an observed effect to a cause \emph{actual causality}. That task description
does not, by itself, specify a formal criterion for an individual's actual
cause. Its smallpox case asks which source produces more deaths in a stipulated
population. With the given numbers, vaccination reactions produce
$990{,}000(0.01)(0.01)=99$ deaths, while disease among unvaccinated people
produces $10{,}000(0.02)(0.20)=40$. Those population counts differ from the
per-person risks, $0.0001$ and $0.004$. Confusing a total with a risk is an
estimand error; the arithmetic alone does not establish a general
Simpson-reversal mechanism. These are deductions from the paper's stated
example, not new medical evidence.

The banking analogue is direct. A large customer group can contribute more
defaults while offering a smaller default risk per account. A deposit offer
can increase gross balances without increasing net contribution. An assistant
should state the denominator and economic target before presenting the
answer. The paper's prompts provide useful stress cases for that distinction.
The small scenario set and model configurations do not support a current
ranking of assistants for banking work. We have inspected the published
methods and results; we have not reproduced its model calls or inspected every
supplementary response.

\section{Scale does not remove uncertainty about the answer key}
MDC-Bench broadens the comparison to 8,422 questions across seven disciplines,
including business, economics and management. Its tasks distinguish reasoning,
intervention, decision and counterfactual questions. Questions are constructed
from causal narratives extracted from preprints, with model-generated
alternatives and a manual sampling check. The published protocol identifies
model versions, prompt templates, temperature and output limits.
\citep[Sections 2--3 and Appendix A]{gap29mdc}

Its harder condition requires two ranked answers instead of one. For example,
the reported Claude thinking configuration has average accuracy 84.56\% in
the basic condition and 59.25\% in the harder condition. These are different
response requirements on the same benchmark; their difference is not a
measured deterioration in one fixed banking task. The benchmark is useful
for comparing errors by causal structure and question type, provided its
answer-generation assumptions remain visible.

The detailed prompts reveal an important distinction. Reverse reasoning may
use necessity and sufficiency, or otherwise select an abductive explanation
judged probable from background knowledge. Intervention questions construct
an altered causal narrative; the answer alternatives are ranked by their
judged plausibility. These procedures do not supply a known structural
equation system, a randomised treatment effect or an identified posterior
over causal diagrams. Appendix A's sampling review helps detect poor
questions but does not turn model-generated causal statements into independent
economic truth. The authors also discuss weak long-chain relations and
distractors that may be too easy. \citep[Limitations; Tables 28--29 and
39--40]{gap29mdc}

\section{An agent architecture still needs an identified effect}
Chen combines language models, diffusion models and interacting agents in a
study of climate-policy sentiment. Section 6 describes 43,943 tweets and
comparisons with topic, language and diffusion baselines. It reports F1,
AUC, causal-chain precision, counterfactual error and simulated intervention
outcomes. Table 4 removes individual components to examine their contribution.
These are reported results of the paper; the model was not reproduced
locally. \citep[Sections 5.6 and 6; Tables 1--4]{gap29chen}

The causal interpretation needs more than those comparisons. Equation (16)
factorises a joint distribution according to a graph. Equation (17) defines
a conditional treatment contrast. Neither statement alone identifies that
contrast from the observed tweets. Equation (19) compares predicted and
reference counterfactual outcomes, but its accompanying text allows the
reference to come from annotations or simulated baselines. Section 6.1 does
not supply enough detail to reconstruct an independently identified
counterfactual for each tweet. F1 and AUC assess labelled prediction; they
do not repair that missing identification argument.

The useful proposal lesson is to separate an architecture from the evidence
for a decision. A bank may test whether a language model helps extract a
policy variable or whether a simulator represents a declared mechanism.
It still needs a defensible treatment assignment, observation model and
counterfactual comparison before attributing a financial gain to the policy.
The reported architecture is a research lead. Its stated improvements are
not evidence that the proposed banking service already delivers causal or
commercial benefits.

\section{A useful banking comparison}
The proposal should use such benchmarks to diagnose formulation and reasoning
failures, then add tasks whose consequences can be checked independently.
A compact questionnaire and an executable calculation are necessary
comparators. For a deposit question, all methods should receive the same
decision date, eligibility rule, alternative offer and contribution definition.
For servicing, all should see the same observed history and reasons for
dropout. For a diagram, an admissible set should remain admissible when the
observations cannot orient an edge.

The resulting assessment has distinct outcomes: whether the target is correct,
whether a proposed adjustment is justified, whether an unknown effect remains
unknown, whether the numerical calculation is correct, and how much analyst
time the assistance saves. Independent adjudication is needed for open-ended
economic formulations. Generated cases with known mechanisms can test
specific errors before an expensive bank exercise. The public experimental,
servicing and linkage studies in this volume provide numerical cases of that
kind, but no live assistant has yet been evaluated on them.

The inspected papers therefore sharpen the proposed experiment rather
than establishing a benefit from the proposed service. Repeated agreement
among prompts is especially weak evidence when their errors share a source,
as the repeated-measurement calculation shows. The useful next comparison
measures consequential mistakes and time on held-out tasks, with human
adjudication and a fixed cost allowance.

\section{A conditional recommendation to the sponsor}
The present evidence supports a small, comparative prototype assembled from
existing methods. It does not support a general replacement for the bank's
statistical estate. The comparison should begin with a single offer or rollout
question, a fixed population and information date, a simple estimator and a
documented alternative. Add assistance only where it can be compared with a
questionnaire or conventional research workflow. Include erroneous and
unsupported requests, because avoiding a false recommendation is part of
the expected benefit.

Let $N$ be annual eligible studies, $h$ analyst hours saved per study, $w$ the
fully loaded hourly cost, $D$ the expected reduction in consequential decision
loss per study, $C$ annual operating cost and $K$ the annualised development
and adoption cost. A provisional annual net benefit is
\[
 B=N(wh+D)-C-K.
\]
This is an accounting framework, not an estimate. Avoid double-counting
correction hours in both $h$ and $D$. Costs include unsuccessful studies,
training, interpretation and maintenance. Benefits must be measured against
the bank's feasible existing workflow. No observed values for these terms
are available in the new study, so a numerical return on investment would
be invented.

The next expenditure should buy information about those terms: a matched
analyst study using public or generated cases, with fixed questions, independent
judgement of the resulting analysis and recorded time. A credible gain would
justify a narrowly scoped bank-data pilot. Equal quality and cost would favour
improving the existing workflow. Frequent unsupported assumptions would favour
better data or a different intervention design. These alternatives let the
proposal make progress before expensive authentic-bank validation, while
keeping the eventual investment decision conditional on evidence.

\chapter{The investment case and its alternatives}
\label{r3:investment}

A common causal product earns its cost by improving repeated scientific
work. The appropriate alternative is a capable quantitative team composing
the same open-source methods with ordinary engineering, documentation and
review. Such a team can produce good causal studies without a new platform.
The investment question is whether the shared representations and qualified
operations reduce the cost of equivalent work or enable additional valuable
decisions, after construction, support and adoption are included.

\section{Define equivalent output before pricing reuse}
\label{r3:equivalent-output}

An equivalent completed study has a reconstructed population and observation
clock, a clear intervention and financial outcome, a defensible identification
argument or useful nonidentification conclusion, appropriate inference,
reproducible artifacts and review. The comparison must include negative
results. An early finding that a requested target is unidentified can save
substantial work; forcing every study to return a numerical effect would
reward scientific error.

The proposed service would help analysts reconstruct what was known when
a decision was made, keep the population and outcome consistent, document
why an effect is identified, and carry uncertainty into the financial
comparison. It would reuse existing numerical methods where their
assumptions fit. Each business would still specify its products, costs and
constraints. A mortgage policy, an individual collections decision and a
macroeconomic shock need not share the same economic quantity of interest.

Comparator costs should include the same required outputs and review
quality. Reduced effort from omitting uncertainty or failing to investigate
weak support is not a saving. Conversely, building a generic model interface
for a one-off study can cost more than a small, clearly documented expert
analysis. The portfolio of genuinely repeated requests, not the total
number of database rows, determines the economic opportunity.

\section{An auditable cost model}
\label{r3:cost-model}

For alternative $j\in\{E,P\}$, expert composition or shared product,
let $K_j$ be initial construction cost, $F_j$ annual shared cost,
$c_j$ marginal cost per equivalent completed study, and $n_t$ completed
studies in year $t$. With horizon $H$ and discount rate $r$,
\begin{equation}
 C_j=K_j+\sum_{t=1}^{H}\frac{F_j+c_jn_t}{(1+r)^t}.
 \label{r3:present-cost}
\end{equation}
The categories are disjoint: method maintenance and common infrastructure
belong in $F_j$, while study-specific preparation, fitting, review and
rework belong in $c_j$. Failed-study costs must be included in one
category; a completed-study denominator cannot make them disappear.

Use the following illustrative USD-million assumptions to expose the
break-even logic:
\[
 (K_E,F_E,c_E)=(1,.6,.15),\qquad
 (K_P,F_P,c_P)=(4,1.8,.06),\qquad H=3,\quad r=.10.
\]
These are planning inputs, not observed bank prices, measured productivity
or enterprise vendor quotations. Let
$a_H=\sum_{t=1}^H(1+r)^{-t}$. At constant annual volume $n$, the cost-only
threshold, when $c_E>c_P$, is
\begin{equation}
 n^*=\frac{(K_P-K_E)/a_H+(F_P-F_E)}{c_E-c_P}.
 \label{r3:reuse-threshold}
\end{equation}
If the marginal saving is zero or negative, this particular reuse argument
does not establish a positive-volume crossover. Under the stipulated
numbers, $a_H=2.48685$ and $n^*=26.74$ studies annually.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small
\input{writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/3a8f90066fa1af4f.tex}
\caption{Three-year present cost in illustrative USD millions. Annual
volumes are 8, 24 and 36, or the ramp $(4,16,30)$. Both alternatives
deliver the same specified scientific outputs.}
\label{r3:reuse-economics}
\end{table}

At eight annual studies the product costs about USD\,4.19 million more.
At 24 it still costs about USD\,.61 million more. At 36 it saves about
USD\,2.07 million. The ramp leaves a USD\,2.44 million premium even
though final-year volume exceeds the constant-volume threshold:
construction occurs before most reuse. Halving marginal savings doubles
the threshold to 53.47 studies; increasing the annual shared-cost
premium to USD\,2 million raises it to 35.63.

\begin{figure}[htbp]\centering
\includegraphics[width=.88\textwidth]{derivations/reuse_economics.pdf}
\caption{The crossover follows from the declared account. It is not
a forecast of demand or evidence that the shared layer already saves effort.}
\end{figure}

The simple model holds study mix fixed. A more realistic portfolio has
classes $k$ with costs $c_{jk}$ and volumes $n_{tk}$, replacing
$c_jn_t$ by $\sum_k c_{jk}n_{tk}$. A few expensive bespoke latent
models may have little shared work with many routine rollouts.
Reuse should therefore be measured by operation and data contract, not
assumed from a common causal-inference label.

\section{Separate business value from construction savings}
\label{r3:incremental-value}

Let $D_t$ be incremental realized decision value attributable to the
product relative to the equivalent expert workflow. Then
\begin{equation}
 \Delta\operatorname{NPV}
 =C_E-C_P+\sum_{t=1}^{H}\frac{D_t}{(1+r)^t}.
 \label{r3:incremental-npv}
\end{equation}
The first term already counts workflow savings. Released analyst time
must not be added again as business value. If it permits extra studies,
their costs, capacity use, outcome lags and incremental decisions
belong in the expanded account.

At 24 annual studies the illustrative cost premium requires about
USD\,.246 million of additional constant annual decision value.
The adoption ramp requires about USD\,.980 million. The size of a
bank's balance sheet does not establish either amount. The expert
comparator may already identify the same profitable policy or reject
the same loss-making offer.

The deposit study illustrates the attribution problem. Finding a
negative contribution can prevent a loss only if the finding changes
what would otherwise have been done. The prevented loss cannot be
credited to the product merely because its report contains the estimate.
Likewise the simulated collections gain is a property of the declared
environment; it supplies no observed revenue to this investment account.
Latent-state research can be worthwhile even while operational value
remains uncertain.

Costs and gains also mature on different clocks. Data access,
implementation and review are paid before customer outcomes are
observed. A six-month retention measure may mature during an early
evaluation; credit losses or a persistent pricing response may not.
A continuation model supplies a conditional forecast for those outcomes,
not an observation. Report the cash timing and model dependence explicitly.

\section{Measure the common-product hypothesis}
\label{r3:adoption-experiment}

The complete-workflow measurements in Section~\ref{s4:workflow-results}
refine the resource account but do not estimate its labor terms. A response
workflow over 3.85 million versioned records takes about 3.38 seconds on the
recorded host; a 3,200-customer latent workflow with 19 bootstrap refits takes
about 48.27 seconds. Both the product and expert-composition arms can use
these same numerical operations. Pricing one arm from a bare estimator call
and the other from reconstruction plus inference would be an unequal-output
comparison. The illustrative per-study dollar inputs above therefore remain
unchanged pending matched measurements of preparation, review and rework.

The first tranche should compare matched tasks in the intervention,
sequential-decision and dynamic-systems workspaces. Agree their outputs,
scientific scope and reviewer rubric before measuring effort. Give the
expert-composition arm the same sources, data access and expertise, and
allow sensible reusable templates. Counterbalance task order where
possible to reduce learning effects.

Measure analyst and reviewer hours, calendar delay, machine cost,
failed starts, rework and unresolved material findings separately.
Ask a second analyst to reconstruct the population, target and financial
conclusion from the exported artifacts. Deliberately introduced clock,
weight and sign errors can test whether review finds the defects.
This tests the proposed product's specific value proposition, rather
than whether a polished interface is pleasant.

A planning target of 30\% lower median analyst/reviewer effort can be
useful if review quality and output scope are held fixed. It remains

review. Such a team can produce good causal studies without a new platform.

operations reduce the cost of equivalent work or enable additional valuable
decisions, after construction, support and adoption are included.

\label{r3:equivalent-output}

clock, a clear intervention and financial outcome, a defensible identification

results. An early finding that a requested target is unidentified can save
substantial work; forcing every study to return a numerical effect would
reward scientific error.

assumptions fit. Each business would still specify its products, costs and
constraints. A mortgage policy, an individual collections decision and a
macroeconomic shock need not share the same economic quantity of interest.

quality. Reduced effort from omitting uncertainty or failing to investigate

\label{r3:cost-model}

For alternative $j\in\{E,P\}$, expert composition or shared product,

studies in year $t$. With horizon $H$ and discount rate $r$,
\begin{equation}

 \label{r3:present-cost}
\end{equation}

category; a completed-study denominator cannot make them disappear.

\chapter{When a bank experiment becomes worth its

\hypertarget{proposal-acceptance-and-later-qualification}{%
\section{The evidence needed before investing}\label{proposal-acceptance-and-later-qualification}}

The investment decision requires a comparison of feasible alternatives,
their costs and the evidence for their expected benefits. Reproducible
public and simulated studies can support that comparison within their
stated assumptions. A restricted result may justify a narrow prototype
while leaving broader research questions unresolved.

Public evidence informs three choices: which existing methods to reuse,
where language assistance is useful, and how analysts should conduct a
reproducible study. A dataset can reveal a timing error or support a
controlled comparison without settling every question about those choices.

Later bank qualification asks a different question: do the assumptions,
precision, workflows and economics hold for a specific institution? That
stage may need genuine offer histories, logging information, independent
labels, owner-reviewed semantics, production constraints and prospective
outcomes. The relevant input should be requested only for the capability
and target population under test. An internal bank pilot is not required
to demonstrate that the proposal has a reproducible public baseline and
a sensible experiment design.

\hypertarget{a-value-of-information-decision}{%
\section{A value-of-information
decision}\label{a-value-of-information-decision}}

Let \(d\in\{\text{stop},\text{build},\text{pilot}\}\) denote an
investment choice, \(\theta\) unresolved technical and economic
conditions, and \(U(d,\theta)\) its net value. Let \(E\) denote current
public/prototype evidence and \(Z\) the possible result of a proposed
experiment. A planning expression for the expected value of sample
information is

\[
\operatorname{EVSI}
=\mathbb E_{Z\mid E}\!\left[\max_d\mathbb E\{U(d,\theta)\mid E,Z\}\right]
-\max_d\mathbb E\{U(d,\theta)\mid E\}.
\]

An experiment merits consideration when its expected decision
improvement exceeds its full incremental cost, including data
preparation, customer burden where relevant, security review, labeling,
analyst time and opportunity cost. This is a project decision framework,
not an empirically estimated ROI. Where a probability model for
\(\theta\) is unjustified, use a scenario table and sensitivity bounds
instead of a precise-looking EVSI number.

A simple illustrative calculation shows the sequencing. Suppose, purely
for planning, a small bank study costing 20,000 could avert an
unsuitable 200,000 build in 20\% of scenarios, with no other benefits or
costs. Its gross avoided-spend value would be 40,000 and its net would
be 20,000 under those assumptions. If the study changes the build
decision in only 2\% of scenarios, the same gross value is 4,000 and it
is not justified on that ground. These are stipulated arithmetic
examples, not quotations, bank probabilities or forecasts.

The decision should identify the uncertainty that matters. If a public
benchmark shows repeated action-clock mistakes, improve the formulation
layer before requesting confidential data. If a correct estimator is too
slow on modest data, fix or replace it before commissioning a platform
pilot. If all plausible effects lead to the same action, a costly
precision improvement may have little value. If policy value reverses
when a missing hardship variable is plausible, a carefully scoped bank
measurement study can have high value even when the public-data
implementation is technically sound.

\hypertarget{conditions-for-moving-to-expensive-evidence}{%
\section{Conditions for moving to expensive
evidence}\label{conditions-for-moving-to-expensive-evidence}}

An actionable next-experiment recommendation specifies the proposed
intervention, target population, candidate baseline, decision-loss
threshold and the smallest information addition that could alter the
decision. It also states an explicit stop or redesign outcome. A bank
experiment should not be recommended merely to fill a missing-evidence
cell.

For funding, the missing addition may be time-stamped offers and an
assignment mechanism, not more aggregate deposits. For servicing, it may
be feasible-action and hardship information at each decision time. For
discovery, it may be one feasible intervention that distinguishes
competing graphs. For observation construction, it may be a
representative independently resolved sample of uncertain identities
with known inclusion probabilities. Public data help design each
measurement and estimate its computational burden, while the bank
supplies the later population-specific truth.

Authentic institutional approval, independent acceptance, actual
workflow prices and production service levels remain future
qualification requirements. A proposal can be complete without them. It
cannot honestly claim those outcomes without obtaining them.

\hypertarget{remaining-survey-and-prototype-gaps}{%
\section{Remaining survey and prototype
gaps}\label{remaining-survey-and-prototype-gaps}}

The survey has established a usable portfolio and a concrete public-data
acquisition/profile, not six executed new studies. Current-source web
snapshots still need exact data-file vintages for future analyses.
Several benchmark datasets need data-specific rights checks. Mortgage
histories require registration and use review; the HMDA publication
endpoint was inaccessible in this run. The Criteo license is a material
constraint for a commercial proposal. These affect individual options;
project-generated alternatives and the already local public data keep
the prototype work moving.

No inspected public financial source supplies the complete logged bank
servicing action process or independent real-bank linkage truth. That
finding is limited to the surveyed sources. It calls for transparent
semi-synthetic experiments now and a justified targeted measurement
later, rather than a claim of impossibility. Public reasoning benchmarks
also cannot establish a live agent's quality without an actual
controlled run, nor resolve the business owner's normative choice of
outcome and feasible intervention.

Finally, public data do not repair the open mathematical arguments for
persistent dependence, hidden states, graph-equivalence effect sets or
arbitrary learning procedures. Those questions remain scoped research
obligations. The proposal can present negative findings and restricted
supported regimes, compare alternatives and describe what evidence would
change the recommendation. That is a strong proposal standard without
pretending that an accepted bank product already exists.

\[
 \tau_B=\E[B_i(1)-B_i(0)],\qquad

\]

\begin{equation}
 \tau_C=(m-\Delta r)\tau_B-\Delta r B_0-c.
 \label{rewrite:value-map}
\end{equation}

independent of potential balances within each stratum, with probabilities

\[
 \tau_B=\sum_{x=0}^1 w_x
   \{\E[B\mid Z=1,X=x]-\E[B\mid Z=0,X=x]\},
 \qquad w_0=w_1=\tfrac12.
\]

\chapter{Servicing decisions change the next decision's information}

 P(A_0=1\mid L_0)&=0.2+0.6L_0,\\
 P(L_1=1\mid L_0,A_0)&=0.1+0.5L_0+0.2A_0,\\
 P(A_1=1\mid H_1)&=0.15+0.5L_1+0.1A_0,\\
 Y&=20+3A_0+4A_1+10L_1+6L_0.
\end{align*}

 \psi(a)=20+7a+10(0.35+0.2a)+6(0.5)=26.5+9a.
\]

\chapter{A learned graph can leave the pricing decision unresolved}
\label{rewrite:discovery}

example. Consider the centered Gaussian observational covariance
\[
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}
 1&0.6&0.48\\0.6&1.36&1.088\\0.48&1.088&1.8704
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The law satisfies $X\perp Y\mid M$. A chain $X\to M\to Y$, a
fork $X\leftarrow M\to Y$, and a reverse chain $X\leftarrow M\leftarrow Y$
can all reproduce it using independent Gaussian errors.

For the first chain, take $M=0.6X+\varepsilon_M$ and
$Y=0.8M+\varepsilon_Y$, with variances $\Var(X)=1$,
$\Var(\varepsilon_M)=1$ and $\Var(\varepsilon_Y)=1$. The intervention
slope of $Y$ on $X$ is $0.6(0.8)=0.48$. For the fork, take

with residual variances $1-0.6^2/1.36$ and $1$. The resulting covariance

 \quad\hbox{pounds}.
\]

\chapter{Correcting records can change the action}
\label{rewrite:observation}

A treatment record is a measurement of an event. Let $A$ be true randomized
receipt, $W$ recorded receipt and $Y$ gross contribution in pounds at a
fixed horizon. In this separate finite example, $P(A=0)=P(A=1)=1/2$
and $\E[Y\mid A=0]=100$, $\E[Y\mid A=1]=140$. Receipt is
randomized by construction; correcting its record would not establish
randomization in an observational campaign.

Suppose misclassification is nondifferential with a known matrix
\[
 K=\begin{pmatrix}0.9&0.2\\0.1&0.8\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad K_{wa}=P(W=w\mid A=a,Y).
\]
Writing $p_a=P(A=a)$ and $q_a=\E[Y\mathbf1(A=a)]$, the recorded
shares and outcome moments obey
\[
 p_W=Kp_A=(0.55,0.45)' ,\qquad q_W=Kq_A=(59,61)' .
\]
Thus the recorded contrast is $61/0.45-59/0.55=28.2828\ldots$.
The matrix has determinant $0.7$, so its inverse recovers
$p_A=(0.5,0.5)'$ and $q_A=(50,70)'$, giving the true contrast
$70/0.5-50/0.5=40$. This is the moment version of the joint-law
argument in Chapter~\ref{r3:observation}. It is checked by direct
multiplication and solution, with no estimated audit law.

\section{The value of knowing the observation law}
At a stipulated action cost of \pounds35, the recorded comparison gives
net value about $-\pounds6.72$, whereas the corrected contrast gives
\pounds5. That reversal is conditional on the known error law. If an
identity matrix and the displayed matrix both remain admissible, the same
recorded shares and moments are compatible with different latent effects
and opposite recommendations. Reporting only the corrected number would
replace measurement uncertainty with a convenient assumption.

In a real validation sample, estimating $K$ would add uncertainty. The audit
must identify true receipt and represent the relevant customers and periods;
a classifier's own label is not an external truth measurement. Near-singular
matrices amplify error, and a singular matrix destroys recoverable information.
The retained chapter gives the symmetric-error example where receipt becomes
uninformative. More rows with the same deficient measurement law do not
restore its rank.

Entity linkage poses a related but distinct problem. A household may hold
several accounts, and a mistaken join can change both its treatment and its
outcome. Correctness counts alone may fail to identify the needed contrast;
the detailed linkage studies and their adverse results remain in this book.
The next useful observation is a correctly sampled, truthful linked history
when that is what the estimand requires, not merely a higher aggregate match
score. Likewise, event time, availability time and revision time must remain
separate when constructing a prospective decision view.

The four journeys now imply a common requirement for the proposed service.
It must keep the economic target and the information that identifies it
attached to the numerical result. Their statistical procedures remain
different: stratified assignment contrasts, sequential policy averaging,
model-set propagation and observation-law inversion. The next chapters
develop those differences before the software and investment synthesis chooses
which ones are ready for a bounded comparison.

\]

can become too wide to guide action. The earlier generated study shows why

\eqref{rewrite:value-map} is increasing in $\tau_B$. Its endpoints
therefore transform directly: $I_C=0.0275 I_B-30$. Uncertainty in these

8,000 generated observations give the following actual calculation.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrr}
\toprule Quantity & Estimate & Interval\\\midrule
Annual average balance effect (\pounds) & \DepositEstimate & [\DepositLow, \DepositHigh]\\
Annual contribution per household (\pounds) & \DepositNet & [\DepositNetLow, \DepositNetHigh]\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The four cells contain 2,039 unoffered and 1,961 offered households in the

The positive contribution interval supports the action under this declared
model and expense rule. Its margin is small: an additional certain expense
above the lower endpoint removes that interval-based assurance. The result
is unsuitable as a bank forecast; its value is to make the target, support,
uncertainty and accounting inseparable in the completed report.

\section{What the implemented example actually returns}
The local callable estimator takes the three-column generated data, target
weights, four accounting inputs and $\alpha$. It returns cell counts and
uncertainty, the balance target, its interval, contribution and its interval,
and a conditional decision. The same calculation is available at the command
line from the repository root:
\begin{lstlisting}
python3 tools/run_rewrite_examples_20261029.py --report-only
\end{lstlisting}
The callable result and a separate command-line process agree exactly in
the retained execution. The generated data, code, seed and numerical results
are supplied with the study. This is a specific estimator implemented for
the example; it is not evidence that an external causal package was qualified.

The existing MCP walkthrough separately establishes graph syntax, conditional
adjustment, information-date checks and refusal of a dependent sampling law
through that route. It does not expose this new estimator as an MCP operation.
Chapter~\ref{scisyn:investment} gives the observed requests and the initial
timeout as well as the successful retry. Combining those two observations
into a claim of a completed MCP financial analysis would overstate the work.
A future adapter must carry the complete report, including assumptions and
unsupported outcomes, before that claim becomes available.

Two extensions show what this transparent report leaves to be learned.
Chapter~\ref{gap29:public} estimates an assignment contrast from the retained
public experiment, compares adjusted and unadjusted estimators, examines
influence, and subtracts an explicit cost. Its earnings units and population
are different from the deposit account: the exercise tests an inferential
and reporting route, not transport of an earnings effect into bank balances.
Chapter~\ref{gap29:funding} follows institutions rather than households and
asks whether fixed effects can repair a misassigned outcome. They cannot
recover the institution's identity merely by absorbing a persistent level.
The structural funding and calendar arguments explain the additional shock
and dependence assumptions needed for that journey.

For the offer study, the next source of information is assignment support and
correct household aggregation; for the institutional panel it is a coherent
exposure and outcome history. A bank cannot substitute a successful estimate
in one of these populations for the missing design evidence in the other.
The shared report can preserve both questions without pretending they have
the same estimator or sampling law.

\chapter{Servicing decisions change the next decision's information}
\label{rewrite:servicing}

A servicing policy chooses whether to contact a borrower at two dates. Let
$A_0,A_1$ be contact decisions, $L_0$ baseline borrower state and $L_1$ the
state observed between contacts. For this constructed example, $Y$ is
gross contribution in pounds over the two-period horizon, excluding contact
cost. The policy comparison is sustained contact versus no contact, not
the regression coefficient of one contact conditional on every later event.

The exact law developed in Chapter~\ref{r3:longitudinal} is
\begin{align*}
 P(L_0=1)&=0.5,\\
 P(A_0=1\mid L_0)&=0.2+0.6L_0,\\
 P(L_1=1\mid L_0,A_0)&=0.1+0.5L_0+0.2A_0,\\
 P(A_1=1\mid H_1)&=0.15+0.5L_1+0.1A_0,\\
 Y&=20+3A_0+4A_1+10L_1+6L_0.
\end{align*}
Here $H_1=(L_0,A_0,L_1)$ is the history available for the second action.
Independent innovations implement these kernels. The actions have support
for every possible history, and the example has no hidden confounding.
Consequently, replacing both action kernels with a specified policy and
retaining the state-transition law identifies its mean. This is the
g-formula developed from sequential exchangeability in the retained chapter
and its primary treatment. \citep[Chapter 21]{hernan2020}

\section{Average the state produced by each policy}
For a constant policy $a$, the mean intermediate state is
$\E[L_1(a)]=0.1+0.5(0.5)+0.2a=0.35+0.2a$. Hence
\[
 \psi(a)=20+7a+10(0.35+0.2a)+6(0.5)=26.5+9a.
\]
The gross means are \pounds26.50 and \pounds35.50. At a stipulated
\pounds2 per contact, the net contrast is $9-2(2)=\pounds5$.
The reported exact enumeration independently averages the finite state law
and reweights the observed action paths; both recover the same two means.
There is no finite-sample confidence claim in this calculation.

A regression of $Y$ on all four variables correctly recovers action
coefficients 3 and 4. Their sum misses the extra $10(0.2)=2$ contributed
through the change in $L_1$. Removing $L_1$ from the second-stage regression
does not repair the analysis: the historical second action depends on it.
The calculation therefore distinguishes a fitted conditional equation from
the policy mean obtained by averaging that equation over policy-specific
histories. The distinction changes net value from an erroneous \pounds3
to \pounds5 even in this noise-free conditional outcome model.

\section{What changes when the law must be learned}
In an observed study, the kernels and outcome regressions are estimated.
G-computation substitutes fitted transition and outcome laws and averages
under the target policy. Reweighting instead uses ratios of target to
historical action probabilities. Doubly robust constructions combine these
ideas; their longitudinal scores, nuisance restrictions and remainders are
derived in Chapter~\ref{r3:longitudinal}, rather than assumed from their
name. None removes the requirement that the historical records include
the information responsible for action selection.

For sustained contact, a useful diagnostic is the count and weight
distribution of complete histories supporting that policy. Many borrower
rows do not guarantee enough such histories. A policy learned by maximizing
the same estimated value must be evaluated with the additional selection
uncertainty or an honest evaluation sample. An outcome law conditional on
a hidden state introduces another identification problem; a well-fitting
state-space model does not establish that its intervention meaning is correct.

The product implication is to begin with a fixed, short-horizon policy and
observable histories, retaining a direct g-computation and a weighting
comparison. If support is inadequate or an important action determinant is
unrecorded, changing the collection or trial design is more informative than
adding a flexible learner. The positive \pounds5 example explains the
accounting; it does not establish a real contact policy's benefit.

\section{Estimated policies, missing rewards and decision uncertainty}
Chapters~\ref{gap29:servicing} and \ref{gap29:policy-uncertainty} carry the
policy question into fitted data. They use a separate three-decision economy,
with continuous states and rewards already net of the stipulated action cost.
Those reward units are not the pounds in this two-contact example. Whole
customers, rather than isolated rows, supply the sampling units. A separate
training sample chooses the policy; evaluation and resampling hold that
selected policy fixed.

The fitted comparison is informative precisely because it can fail.
Under its maintained state and observation model, improvement coverage is
94\% with an average interval width of 0.711 reward units. Future-dependent
dropout reduces coverage to 6\%; omitting a state predictor reduces it to
61\%. These observed fractions have Monte Carlo uncertainty, reported in
the study. They demonstrate that resampling an estimated model does not
repair an invalid observation assumption.

The financial interpretation follows the reward definition. Where costs are
already subtracted, subtracting contact cost again would double-count it.
Where a bank's reward law and initial distribution must also be estimated,
the supplied-law components of the generated comparison cannot be treated
as known. Outcome follow-up, action support and measured decision history
therefore determine whether its narrower uncertainty can be useful.

\chapter{A learned graph can leave the pricing decision unresolved}
\label{rewrite:discovery}

Suppose $X$ measures a proposed rate change in percentage points, $M$ an
intermediate market quantity and $Y$ gross funding contribution in thousands
of pounds. The units and coefficients in this section are authored for the
example. Consider the centered Gaussian observational covariance
\[
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}
 1&0.6&0.48\\0.6&1.36&1.088\\0.48&1.088&1.8704
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The law satisfies $X\perp Y\mid M$. A chain $X\to M\to Y$, a
fork $X\leftarrow M\to Y$, and a reverse chain $X\leftarrow M\leftarrow Y$
can all reproduce it using independent Gaussian errors.

For the first chain, take $M=0.6X+\varepsilon_M$ and
$Y=0.8M+\varepsilon_Y$, with variances $\Var(X)=1$,
$\Var(\varepsilon_M)=1$ and $\Var(\varepsilon_Y)=1$. The intervention
slope of $Y$ on $X$ is $0.6(0.8)=0.48$. For the fork, take
$\Var(M)=1.36$, $X=(0.6/1.36)M+\eta_X$, and $Y=0.8M+\eta_Y$,
with residual variances $1-0.6^2/1.36$ and $1$. The resulting covariance
is the same, but intervening on $X$ has zero effect on $Y$. The reverse
chain uses the corresponding conditional regression coefficients and also
has zero effect. The numerical check reconstructs all three covariance
matrices and verifies positive residual variances.

\section{Keep the causal ambiguity in the financial report}
Within this specified three-model family, the slope set is $\{0,0.48\}$.
At a quarter-point intervention and a stipulated \pounds60 action cost,
net value is
\[
 1000(0.25)\{0,0.48\}-60=\{-60,60\}
 \quad\hbox{pounds}.
\]
There is no sign-robust recommendation across the retained explanations.
Returning the slope from the forward chain alone would hide the unresolved
orientation that determines the action. A probability for each graph would
require additional justified modelling; equal probabilities are not supplied
by observational equivalence. Nor should the discrete set be called a
confidence interval. It represents identification ambiguity even if the
covariance is known exactly.

The example's finite graph family and linear Gaussian law are restrictions.
They do not describe every model compatible with arbitrary banking records.
When the covariance and graph class are estimated, uncertainty must cover
both the observed law and the retained models before mapping them to effects.
An edge bootstrap conditional on one chosen graph does not supply that
combined guarantee. The foundations and detailed temporal-discovery
comparisons retain the arguments for unresolved orientations, latent causes
and class-to-effect propagation.

For a bank, useful additional information could be a defensible ordering
that excludes two orientations, a valid instrument, or an intervention on
$X$. The cost of obtaining that information should be compared with the
consequence of a mistaken action. More precise estimation of this same
covariance cannot distinguish these three laws. The proposed service should
therefore preserve a class or explicit refusal and ask what would narrow it,
instead of completing arrows solely to make a diagram look decisive.

\section{From a known covariance to estimated effect sets}
Chapter~\ref{exec13:temporal-region} supplies the next inferential step under
a restricted stationary Gaussian time-series model. It constructs a region
jointly over the observed covariance, a continuous unknown common lag and a
declared family of causal models, then maps that region to effects. The
coverage argument keeps the true model and observed-law uncertainty together;
it does not condition on an orientation chosen for convenience. The chapter
also shows what a direct intervention can add.

This is a developed restricted construction, not an executed general
bank-discovery pipeline. The maintained graph family, scalar lag and
innovation law must be defensible before applying it. An unrestricted latent
model may leave the whole line admissible. In the opening pricing example,
the narrower set already contains opposite net values, so a more elaborate
estimator is useful only if its information or restrictions can resolve a
consequential ambiguity. A labelled whole-line result can be the correct
answer to a well-defined question.

\chapter{Correcting records can change the action}
\label{rewrite:observation}

A treatment record is a measurement of an event. Let $A$ be true randomized
receipt, $W$ recorded receipt and $Y$ gross contribution in pounds at a
fixed horizon. In this separate finite example, $P(A=0)=P(A=1)=1/2$
and $\E[Y\mid A=0]=100$, $\E[Y\mid A=1]=140$. Receipt is
randomized by construction; correcting its record would not establish
randomization in an observational campaign.

Suppose misclassification is nondifferential with a known matrix
\[
 K=\begin{pmatrix}0.9&0.2\\0.1&0.8\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad K_{wa}=P(W=w\mid A=a,Y).
\]
Writing $p_a=P(A=a)$ and $q_a=\E[Y\mathbf1(A=a)]$, the recorded
shares and outcome moments obey
\[
 p_W=Kp_A=(0.55,0.45)' ,\qquad q_W=Kq_A=(59,61)' .
\]
Thus the recorded contrast is $61/0.45-59/0.55=28.2828\ldots$.
The matrix has determinant $0.7$, so its inverse recovers
$p_A=(0.5,0.5)'$ and $q_A=(50,70)'$, giving the true contrast
$70/0.5-50/0.5=40$. This is the moment version of the joint-law
argument in Chapter~\ref{r3:observation}. It is checked by direct
multiplication and solution, with no estimated audit law.

\section{The value of knowing the observation law}
At a stipulated action cost of \pounds35, the recorded comparison gives
net value about $-\pounds6.72$, whereas the corrected contrast gives
\pounds5. That reversal is conditional on the known error law. If an
identity matrix and the displayed matrix both remain admissible, the same
recorded shares and moments are compatible with different latent effects
and opposite recommendations. Reporting only the corrected number would
replace measurement uncertainty with a convenient assumption.

In a real validation sample, estimating $K$ would add uncertainty. The audit
must identify true receipt and represent the relevant customers and periods;
a classifier's own label is not an external truth measurement. Near-singular
matrices amplify error, and a singular matrix destroys recoverable information.
The retained chapter gives the symmetric-error example where receipt becomes
uninformative. More rows with the same deficient measurement law do not
restore its rank.

Entity linkage poses a related but distinct problem. A household may hold
several accounts, and a mistaken join can change both its treatment and its
outcome. Correctness counts alone may fail to identify the needed contrast;
the detailed linkage studies and their adverse results remain in this book.
The next useful observation is a correctly sampled, truthful linked history
when that is what the estimand requires, not merely a higher aggregate match
score. Likewise, event time, availability time and revision time must remain
separate when constructing a prospective decision view.

The four journeys now imply a common requirement for the proposed service.
It must keep the economic target and the information that identifies it
attached to the numerical result. Their statistical procedures remain
different: stratified assignment contrasts, sequential policy averaging,
model-set propagation and observation-law inversion. The next chapters
develop those differences before the software and investment synthesis chooses
which ones are ready for a bounded comparison.

\section{A fitted linkage analysis needs an external information budget}
Chapter~\ref{gap29:observation} studies a different observation problem:
matching randomized participants to outcomes when identifiers are corrupted.
It compares exact and fuzzy rules, keeps unmatched customers in the target,
and derives a contribution bound when at most a supplied number of candidate
lists omit the true match. Sampling uncertainty is then added under explicit
support and assignment assumptions. This is not an estimate of the receipt
matrix used above; the two studies concern different measurement mechanisms.

At 30\% outcome-dependent corruption, the robust population interval averages
119.1 outcome units in width, compared with about 4.1 for the fuzzy analysis.
The extra width prices justified ignorance. The corruption budget and outcome
support are external premises, not quantities learned from matching confidence.
A monetary decision first maps those outcome units and bounds into its own
expense equation. When the admissible set straddles that decision threshold,
an independently resolved audit sample can be more valuable than a forced
match. The detailed history and audit studies retain the further complications
of dependent records and uncertain audit truth.
