\chapter{Choosing the capabilities worth assembling}
\label{scisyn:software}

A bank does not buy an average treatment effect. It buys a better decision:
which customers to contact, which price to quote, which branches to reorganise,
or which experiment to fund. Software is useful when its answer bears on that
decision and its assumptions are credible in the setting. A method that answers
a narrower question accurately can be more valuable than an ambitious system
whose output is difficult to interpret.

The detailed comparisons in this monograph support selective reuse. The first
proposal should assemble a small number of named statistical procedures around
a common description of the decision. It should retain a second implementation
where disagreement could expose a consequential mistake. It should not promise
to reproduce every package in one language. The development expense of such a
rewrite is certain; the benefit remains to be demonstrated.

The comparison below draws on the retained technical sources and their dated
versions. It is a synthesis of those inspections, not a new census of current
releases. Research coverage ends on 7 October 2026; acquisition after that date
does not establish historical availability of a mutable manual. A documented
procedure, an executed example and a proposed integration are different kinds
of evidence. Commercial tools are compared by their documented procedures;
unobserved functions remain unknown rather than being treated as absent.

\section{Discovering relationships and identifying effects}

\subsection{1. Discovery from independent observations}
For a cross-sectional customer study, the first choice is the set of assumptions
under which conditional independence or a score can reveal useful structure.
The inspected R pcalg, Python causal-learn and Java Tetrad implementations provide
concrete comparison routes for PC. They expose choices about independence tests,
search and orientation. Using the same algorithm name does not align those
choices. A graph with unresolved directions is a legitimate result, not an
unfinished diagram to be completed by managerial intuition.
\citep{exec13_pcalg_reuse_primary,v12_sw_causallearn,exec13_java_tetrad}

A restricted PC comparison needs one primary implementation and another
whose choices can be inspected independently. The independence test, sampling
unit, significance level and treatment of orientation conflicts determine
whether their outputs can be compared.
Porting the search into a new language is not justified by the proposal's
present evidence. Score-based, functional and continuous-optimisation methods
belong beside PC as different modelling choices, rather than votes for a
majority graph. In particular, agreement among bridges to the same underlying
engine is not independent corroboration. The software recommendation changes
if the bank needs a mixed-data model, hidden common causes or repeated records:
those needs require a separate statistical comparison before an interface is
chosen.

\subsection{2. Hidden common causes, selection and equivalent graphs}
An apparent connection between contact and repayment may arise because staff
recognise distress that the database does not record. Under such circumstances
an analysis assuming no hidden common causes can be precise about the wrong
model. The inspected discovery sources distinguish procedures such as PC and
FCI and different graph representations. An algorithmic orientation conflict
must not be reinterpreted as an established hidden common cause merely because
the display uses a similar pair of arrowheads.
\citep{v12_sw_causallearn,exec13_pcalg_reuse_primary}

The partially directed or ancestral graph determines a range of intervention
conclusions under its stated assumptions. A latent-variable route also needs
an explicit interpretation of its endpoints. Selecting one convenient
orientation would instead report an unidentified effect as identified. This is a rejection of an inference, not of a software
family. Where observationally equivalent models imply different lending
decisions, additional timing knowledge or experimental information is the
valuable purchase. Another graph visualiser cannot supply that information.

\subsection{3. Time, interventions and changing regimes}
Repeated customer observations contain both persistence and common shocks.
The retained Tigramite sources distinguish discovery methods, tests, lag
conventions, graph classes and effect calculations conditional on a supplied
graph. Their observation and masking rules matter when a calendar period is
missing. A row after a missing month is not necessarily the next economic
period. Commercial dynamic-network and structural time-series routes are
useful alternatives, but a supplied temporal model and a discovered model
answer different questions.
\citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec13_ct_genie_dbn,exec13_ct_stata_svar}

Temporal integration therefore depends on the original calendar, observation
availability and the allowed intervention. Evidence from multiple regimes
has a different interpretation from an assumption that one stationary regime
describes all years. A rate change during a funding crisis need not have the response seen
in ordinary months. A lagged prediction improvement alone does not identify a general temporal
effect. The first comparison should assess whether plausible
lag and regime choices change the decision, with graph ambiguity carried into
the effect calculation.

\subsection{4. Adjustment, identification and counterfactual questions}
The bank must distinguish identification of an intervention distribution from
evaluation of a structural model that somebody has supplied. Ananke's inspected
identification and model-oracle interfaces make this distinction concrete.
aGrUM and pyAgrum likewise combine graphical, symbolic and numerical facilities
whose individual meanings must be preserved. A symbolic expression may still
require conditional distributions unsupported by the observed population.
\citep{exec24_ananke_source,exec19_cxx_identification_source,exec24_agrum_source}

Symbolic identification determines what can be learned before an estimator
is selected. Model-based counterfactual simulation answers a separate question
conditional on the supplied structure. A simulation from that structure
therefore cannot establish identification from observational records.
An R, Python or C++ route is acceptable only if it preserves the query,
conditioning set, hidden-variable assumptions and support requirements. The
unresolved commercial comparison concerns exact query semantics and supported
model classes; a capability label such as causal analysis is insufficient.

\section{Estimating benefits from actions and repeated policies}

\subsection{5. Average and heterogeneous effects}
EconML's residual-regression formulation illustrates why the final effect model
matters as much as the prediction methods used to remove confounding. In a
binary-treatment setting with sufficient observed adjustment information $S$,
write $e(S)=P(A=1\mid S)$ and $\tau(S)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid S]$. With exact nuisance
functions and a constant final coefficient, the population projection is
\[
 \theta_* = \frac{E[e(S)\{1-e(S)\}\tau(S)]}
                   {E[e(S)\{1-e(S)\}]}.
\]
The average benefit for the target population is instead $E[\tau(S)]$.
These coincide under a constant effect, but need not do so otherwise. This
derivation concerns a restricted specification, not every EconML estimator.
\citep{exec19_econml_source}

An explicit specification separates adjustment variables, effect modifiers
and population weights before an existing estimator is used.
R forest and targeted-estimation routes and Python DML routes should be compared
on the same population and intervention, not on their default output names.
The inspected grf source gives a concrete R/native reference, while commercial
Stata CATE procedures provide an additional documented comparator.
\citep{exec13_grf_rpath,exec13_ch_stata}
The proposed service's contribution is to make these choices visible and
repeatable. It has not demonstrated predictive or causal superiority over the
existing estimators. The generated study in Chapter~\ref{scisyn:evidence} examines
the decision consequence of an omitted effect modifier.

\subsection{6. Experiments, instruments and discontinuities}

designs than adjustment alone. The inspected commercial IV manuals and
rdrobust sources provide useful estimation and diagnostic comparators.
Their identifying premises remain substantive: a valid excluded instrument
requires an argument about the outcome, and a discontinuity requires a
credible comparison at the threshold. Bias correction for an RD estimate does
not establish a strong first stage for a fuzzy design.
\citep{exec13_ivrd_stata,exec13_ivrd_sas,exec13_ivrd_rdrobust}

calculation. A weak or uninformative result may be correct. Converting an
instrument coefficient into a portfolio-wide effect instead requires an
additional argument connecting the relevant population. The first

\section{What the commercial comparison changes}
Commercial statistical packages are credible alternatives, not an empty space
waiting for the proposed service. The inspected Stata procedures cover distinct
treatment, panel, survival and structural questions; the SAS sources distinguish
statistical procedures from service access. The bank may already possess
trained staff and relevant entitlements. A proposal that ignores those assets
overstates the saving from a new platform.
\citep{exec13_ci_stata_causal_intro,exec18_gp_stata_xthdid,
exec14_survival_stata,exec13_ivrd_sas,exec23_workflow_sasctl}

Compare three feasible alternatives: improve existing analytical practice;
connect a small set of existing procedures; or build a broader common service.
For each study, distinguish a vendor-authored procedure, a community extension
inside a commercial host, an open client to a licensed server, and a general
numerical component. They have different support and cost implications. The
comparison has not established exact current prices, complete entitlements,
performance at the bank's scale or the absence of equivalent features in all
competitors. Those are unresolved commercial questions, not findings of
technical superiority.

The proposed investment is therefore conditional. Its candidate contribution
is a disciplined connection between the business question, assumptions,
software choices and financial interpretation. Fund a narrow comparison that
can show whether that connection prevents material errors or saves analyst
time. If the existing estate achieves the same result more cheaply, retain it.
If differences in estimands, graph interpretation or information dates repeatedly
change decisions, a shared service becomes more persuasive.

\subsection{Reuse the estimator after choosing the population}
For an offer made once to each customer, the relevant average may cover all
eligible customers or only those who actually received the offer. DoubleML's
inspected Python interactive-regression implementation distinguishes these
targets, checks for a single binary treatment, and directs instrumental-variable
data to a different model. It forms separate predictions under treatment and
control, processes the propensity estimates, and constructs the corresponding
score. These are useful reasons to integrate the selected original procedure
instead of writing another implementation merely to change language.

BSD-3-Clause licence and dependencies are recorded separately from the earlier
installed-version observation. \citep{exec23_doubleml_reuse_source}

unadjusted or transparent adjusted comparison retained. Neither the choice of
predictor nor clipping a propensity establishes that every customer had a
realistic chance of receiving each action. Sampling dependence, permissible
covariates, target weights and the uncertainty calculation must agree with the
study. The full distribution and matched adverse-data trials belong in the
prototype comparison. Porting is justified only if a measured platform or
cost constraint outweighs the burden of maintaining the statistical procedure.

effects for an adoption cohort at a particular date, followed by an explicitly
chosen aggregation. The newly retrieved DESCRIPTION comes from the same

identity uncertainty. This is a repository version, not evidence of a stable
published release or of a complete deployment entitlement. A request for a
separate LICENSE file returned 404; that does not cancel the declaration.
\citep{survey29did,exec24_panelr_did}

The source's treatment of time-varying weights matters economically. In a
balanced panel the default comparison uses the earlier period's weights;
choosing varying weights switches to the repeated-cross-section estimator.
In an unbalanced panel, fixing weights at an anchor date restricts the sample
to units observed then. Thus two analysts can agree on the branch records yet
answer different questions after selecting different weighting rules. Imagine
two equally weighted customer groups with hypothetical effects of 10 and
$-10$ units. Their equally weighted effect is zero. If the analysis gives
the first group weight three and the second weight one, the weighted effect
is $(3\times10-10)/4=5$. This is a constructed arithmetic example, not a
\texttt{did} run: changing weights alone changes the population conclusion.
\citep{survey29didapi}

cohort, calendar, weighting and confidence-band definitions. A Python or

The inspected \texttt{causaleffect} documentation describes a symbolic answer
for an intervention distribution, optionally conditional on specified variables.
It returns a formula or structured probability expression when the query is
identified under the supplied graph; a nonidentification path reports the
graphical obstruction. The graph convention represents hidden common causes
through specially marked edges. Its selected source is version 1.3.17 at
ff6059f; the package Date field and commit timestamp disagree, so that
revision is described by its exact saved identity. \citep{exec18_rid_causaleffect}

This supports a bounded role as an identification reference alongside the
chosen graph representation. It does not choose the bank's causal graph,

preserve variable names, hidden-edge marks and the distinction between an
unidentified effect and a computation that failed. Ananke or aGrUM can remain
alternatives where their documented query and hidden-variable semantics match.
There is no scientific reason to port the symbolic algorithm until a concrete
constraint makes the original implementation unsuitable.

\label{sec:exec28-rl}
Reinforcement learning can search for a causal graph without establishing that the graph is identified.
For a bank considering early reminders, the graph-search problem is to compare possible relations
among eligibility,reminder assignment,repayment and recorded customer characteristics. This is
different from learning a servicing policy that will act on customers. In the discovery methods
reviewed here, the reinforcement learner is an optimizer: its actions generate graphs or variable
orders, and a statistical score supplies a reward. A better search can improve a score while
leaving the information needed for a causal effect unchanged. Public or generated data can test
the search and interface contracts before costly bank experiments, provided the score's assumptions
and the target graph are declared separately.~\citep{exec28_rl_zhu,exec28_rl_wang}

penalties. Their model discussion assumes scalar structural equations with jointly independent
additive noises,causal minimality and independently sampled observations. The paper explicitly
recognizes that further restrictions are needed for unique graph identification; its selected
experiments use identifiable families. Its encoder-decoder proposes adjacency matrices,and the
best-scoring sampled graph is the output of the search. Those statements do not establish validity
under a latent common cause,a persistent panel or unmeasured selection into reminders. In a
banking application, such features must be represented or restricted before the graph score can
be interpreted scientifically.~\citep{exec28_rl_zhu}

Wang and coauthors instead search variable orderings. Each complete ordering defines a fully
connected acyclic candidate; variable selection subsequently removes edges. Their sequential
decoder masks previously selected nodes,and the paper distinguishes episodic and dense rewards.
The consistency discussion assumes an identifiable structural equation model and a suitable
distribution family. Its proposition explains why an ordering-compatible model reproducing the
same distribution must cover the true graph under those assumptions. It does not guarantee
global optimization by policy gradients; the paper explicitly discusses local convergence and
approximation. Ordering removes a combinatorial acyclicity burden from the candidate construction,
but does not remove misspecification,finite-sample selection error or causal nonidentification.
Attention in an encoder is a representation mechanism,not an edge-confidence or identification
certificate.~\citep{exec28_rl_wang}

\subsection{A precise qualification at the penalty boundary}
For a graph $G$ with binary adjacency matrix $A$,write $S(G)$ for the score to minimize and
$h(A)=\operatorname{tr}(e^A)-d$ for the nonnegative cycle measure on $d$ nodes. The graph-search
formulation adds $\lambda_1\mathbf{1}\{G\notin\mathcal D\}+\lambda_2h(A)$,where $\mathcal D$
is the set of DAGs. Proposition1 in the inspected Zhu preprint gives the non-strict condition
\[

\]

$h_{\min}>0$ the smallest cycle measure over cyclic candidates. Its proof establishes that an
optimal DAG cannot be beaten by a cyclic candidate under this bound. At equality,however,that

\section{Python identification: the question determines the reusable capability}
\label{exec18:pyid-question}

A lending analyst may ask whether changing an offer improves average repayment,
or whether a particular customer who failed to repay would have succeeded under
another offer. These questions share variables but require different information.
Let $A$ be a binary intervention and $Y(a)$ the repayment outcome under its
assignment to $a$. An average contrast $E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}$ uses two marginal
intervention distributions. The retrospective question
$P\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y=0\}$ also links the factual outcome to that person's
unobserved outcome under another assignment. A package capable of computing the
first quantity does not thereby identify the second. Nor does a representation
of a counterfactual variable establish an algorithm for identifying its law.
The distinction changes the proposed product boundary: a request must state its
query class and available information before an engine is selected.
\citep{exec13_y0_dsl,exec18_pyid_contract}

\subsection{Four complementary source boundaries}
\label{exec18:pyid-packages}

The inspected DoWhy revision separates model specification, identification and
estimation. Its identification method chooses between an ID identifier and an
automatic identifier. It can also construct a graph from supplied inputs, so
the proposed banking route requires an explicit reviewed graph instead of
treating that convenience as elicitation evidence. In the selected revision,
the function assigns the \texttt{proceed\_when\_unidentifiable} option but does
not forward it to either identifier; validation must inspect the returned
estimand and assumptions. This is a static source finding, not a demonstrated
runtime failure. Optional reuse of the pinned identification boundary remains
the preferred initial path. Section~\ref{sec:exec24-gcm-reuse} supplies the
separate GCM source review, including its structural assumptions and
factual-noise reconstruction. Its narrower reference-only decision does not
inherit qualification from this identification interface.
\citep{exec13_dowhy}

The selected pgmpy adjustment interface offers a narrower complementary role:
generation of candidate sets for a specified exposure and outcome. Candidate
generation must be followed by independent causal validation. The reviewed
implementation checks exposure parents in a way that can accept a supplied
mediator set when the exposure has no parents; its \texttt{minimal\_variance}
branch is advertised but raises \texttt{NotImplementedError}. An adapter must
exclude that branch and validate the chosen total-effect adjustment criterion.
Neither a minimal separator nor a successful role check guarantees a globally
minimum-variance adjustment set. These restrictions do not establish anything
about uninspected pgmpy modules.~\citep{exec13_pgmpy_reuse_primary}

The pinned y0 implementation gives a symbolic ADMG identification route.
Its conditional algorithm invokes a rule-2 exchange test and otherwise
normalizes an identified joint distribution. The inspected separation path has
the previously developed bidirected-collider counterexample: conditioning on
the collider can give probability $9/10$, whereas replacing the relevant
variable by intervention gives $1/2$. The proposed native conditional path
therefore remains disabled. Identifying the joint distribution and then
normalizing is a possible restricted alternative when that joint is identified
and its denominator is positive. This sufficient route is not a completeness
claim for conditional identification: failure to identify the entire joint
does not prove failure to identify a particular conditional target.
\citep{exec13_y0_id,exec13_y0_idc,exec13_y0_rule2,exec13_y0_separation,exec13_y0_oracles}

Ananke adds a differently organized source reference. The selected authentic
\texttt{ananke-causal} 0.5.0 distribution was uploaded on 5 December 2023; it is
not presented as the newest release. Its \texttt{OneLineID} object fixes
intervention vertices, finds relevant outcome ancestors and checks whether
each district's kernel can be obtained by fixing other vertices. The \texttt{id()}
method returns a Boolean. The \texttt{functional()} method returns a string
describing the fixing expression and prints fixing-order diagnostics. That
string is not yet a typed portable expression, a fitted estimator or an
uncertainty statement. Proposed reuse would preserve variable identities,
sums, products and fixing operations in a restricted expression representation;
it would never evaluate arbitrary returned text as program code.
\citep{exec18_pyid_one_line,exec18_pyid_contract}

Ananke's experimental identification variants also show why exception names
cannot be the scientific result contract. \texttt{OneLineAID} raises
\texttt{NotIdentifiedError} when the experimental graphs fail its ancestral
precondition; \texttt{OneLineGID} uses the same exception for nonconforming
experimental graphs. A precondition failure must be distinguished from a
valid query proved nonidentified in a declared model class. The source's
supplied-model witness routines compare observational marginals and
interventional distributions of two supplied models. They do not establish
automatic witness construction for every query or arbitrary cross-world
identification.~\citep{exec18_pyid_one_line}

Other Ananke components answer different questions. Its oracle intervenes in a
supplied true model and explicitly states that identification is not considered.
Conditional normalization inside that oracle cannot be cited as identification
from observed data. The missing-data routine addresses full-law identification
with explicit \texttt{R\_} and \texttt{X\_} naming and colluding-path checks.
The \texttt{CausalEffect} estimation interface targets the average contrast
$E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}$ and selects among adjustment-, primal- and nested-fixability
strategies. A file named \texttt{counterfactual\_mean.py} is therefore evidence
about that average-effect interface, not a guarantee for a customer's joint
potential outcomes.~\citep{exec18_pyid_oracle,exec18_pyid_missing,exec18_pyid_mean}

\subsection{What even a randomized study leaves undetermined}
\label{exec18:pyid-coupling}

Consider an exact illustrative population, rather than a fitted bank dataset.
Let $A$ and a latent response type $U$ be independent fair binary variables,
and impose consistency $Y=Y(A)$ and no interference. In the stable model
$Y(0)=U$ and $Y(1)=U$. In the switching model $Y(0)=U$ and $Y(1)=1-U$.
Both are compatible with an allowed $A\to Y$ causal model when faithfulness
is not imposed. The first has no individual response to assignment; in the
second, improvements and harms cancel in the mean. Direct enumeration gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 P(A=a,Y=y)&=\tfrac14 &&(a,y\in\{0,1\}),\\
 P\{Y(0)=1\}&=P\{Y(1)=1\}=\tfrac12,\\
 E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}&=0.
\end{aligned}
\label{exec18:pyid-equal-laws}
\end{equation}
Thus an arbitrarily large randomized study can recover the marginal laws in
this example without identifying their within-person coupling. Among factual
untreated failures, $A=0,Y=0$ implies $U=0$. The stable model then has
$Y(1)=0$, whereas the switching model has $Y(1)=1$. Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 P\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y=0\}=
 \begin{cases}0,&\text{stable model},\\1,&\text{switching model}.\end{cases}
\label{exec18:pyid-conditional}
\end{equation}
Both conditioning events have probability $1/4$, so this disagreement is not
created by conditioning on an impossible event. Exact rational enumeration
retains the complete observed and response-type tables for both models.
\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling}

The ambiguity can be described sharply. Write $p_{ij}=P\{Y(0)=i,Y(1)=j\}$
and let $t=p_{01}$ be the proportion helped by the intervention. The two
marginal constraints and normalization force
\begin{equation}
 (p_{00},p_{01},p_{10},p_{11})
   =\left(\tfrac12-t,t,t,\tfrac12-t\right),
 \qquad 0\leq t\leq\tfrac12.
\label{exec18:pyid-sharp}
\end{equation}
Nonnegativity gives the necessary interval. Conversely, for every $t$ in that
interval, take a latent variable with these four response-type probabilities
and randomize $A$ independently. The resulting structural model attains the
same observed law and intervention marginals. This construction proves
attainability of every interior point as well as both endpoints. Therefore
$P\{Y(1)=1,Y(0)=0\}$ has sharp bounds $[0,1/2]$, and randomization yields
\begin{equation}
 P\{Y(1)=1\mid A=0,Y=0\}
 =\frac{p_{01}}{P\{Y(0)=0\}}=2t\in[0,1].
\label{exec18:pyid-bounds}
\end{equation}
This is an identified set under a stated information model, not a confidence
interval. Sampling uncertainty would require a further procedure that accounts
for estimation of the marginal restrictions.~\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling}

Suppose, solely to interpret the target, a successful recovery is worth
USD400 and changing the original intervention costs USD50. The retrospective
conditional net amount is $400(2t)-50$, with sharp range from minus USD50 to
USD350. The two models reverse the sign of this accounting despite identical
average causal effects. This quantity does not establish an implementable
prospective policy: the factual failure used to select the group was not
known before the original assignment. A future servicing decision would need
its own time-indexed action, available history and outcome horizon. The
example motivates a refusal or an explicit identified set, not hindsight-based
deployment.~\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling}

Additional scientific restrictions can change the answer. Monotonicity
$Y(1)\geq Y(0)$ rules out the harmed response type, so $p_{10}=t=0$ under
these equal marginals. It then forces the stable coupling. Randomization alone
does not supply that restriction. Repeated observations, mechanistic evidence
or a richer structural model would have to justify their own connection across
worlds and time; simply collecting more independent assignments does not reveal
both incompatible assignments for the same occasion. The proposed service
must record the added assumption and its scientific owner before narrowing
the set.~\citep{exec18_pyid_coupling,exec18_pyid_contract}

\subsection{Integration choices follow semantics and dependency constraints}
\label{exec18:pyid-integration}

The reuse proposal is deliberately component-specific. DoWhy supplies a
candidate explicit-graph identification boundary. pgmpy supplies candidate
adjustment sets with independent admissibility checks. y0 supplies a candidate
symbolic ID route, with its native conditional path excluded pending a
separation repair. Ananke supplies a district-fixing reference and a possible
isolated comparator. Directly adopting all four packages would not create one
uniform counterfactual service. Porting their source would transfer symbolic,
graph and maintenance obligations to this project without a demonstrated
deployment advantage; it is not selected initially.
\citep{exec13_dowhy,exec13_pgmpy_reuse_primary,exec13_y0_id,exec18_pyid_one_line,exec18_pyid_contract}

There is also a concrete environment conflict. The selected Ananke release
declares NumPy at least1.23 and below2, statsmodels at least0.13.2 and below0.14,
and pgmpy at least0.1.21 and below0.2. The selected DoWhy revision requires
NumPy above2 and statsmodels at least0.14; the selected pgmpy revision declares
NumPy at least2 and statsmodels at least0.14.5. These declared intervals cannot
all be satisfied in one unchanged environment. Separate pinned processes
communicating through a named-variable result contract are a design option,
not a tested environment resolution. Ananke also imports Sympy in the
identification source without explicitly declaring it in the inspected wheel
metadata; whether a resolved transitive dependency supplies it remains to be
checked. No import failure has been observed here.
\citep{exec18_pyid_metadata,exec18_pyid_one_line,exec13_dowhy_project,exec13_pgmpy_reuse_primary}

The proposed boundary validates cycles, node identity, edge type, latent status
and experimental preconditions before dispatch. Ananke's graph constructor
contains segregation and cycle checks, but their presence and the nearby
correctness TODO do not constitute either a qualification or a demonstrated
defect. Engine diagnostics are retained separately from scientific disposition.
An identified expression, an identified set, a model-specific nonidentification
result, an unsupported question, invalid input and an engine failure remain
distinct outcomes. An empty valid adjustment set must not become a failed query,
and an exception must not become a proved impossibility.
\citep{exec18_pyid_graph,exec18_pyid_one_line,exec18_pyid_contract}

Rights are similarly tied to the actual component and distribution. The
selected DoWhy source carries MIT text and y0 carries BSD three-clause text.
The Ananke archive contains two byte-identical Apache2.0 license files, while
its metadata also includes an Other/Proprietary classifier. The conflicting
declarations remain visible for distribution review rather than being silently
resolved by a package badge. Notice retention, modified-file marking where
applicable and dependency-specific obligations belong in the selected
distribution design. Process separation does not settle those questions.
\citep{exec13_dowhy_license,exec13_y0_license,exec18_pyid_license,exec18_pyid_metadata}

This comparison leaves explicit survey work. The selected DoWhy GCM paths
receive their own source review in Section~\ref{sec:exec24-gcm-reuse}; that
review does not complete native qualification or the wider census.
Implementations of general counterfactual identification and Python
partial-identification optimizers still need authenticated technical
sources, model classes and output checks. A solver would need to distinguish
a feasible witness from a certified sharp endpoint; a counterfactual engine
would need to state what structural information permits abduction and coupling.
The four inspected families support the bounded reuse choices described here.
They do not establish exhaustive Python coverage, installed adapters or
qualified banking decisions.~\citep{exec18_pyid_contract}

\section[R mediation and sensitivity contracts]{R mediation and sensitivity: preserving the intervention, the mixture and the unit of uncertainty}
\label{sec:exec25-rmed}

A bank considering a servicing intervention needs to distinguish an improvement
caused by the intervention from an improvement transmitted through a particular
mechanism. Let $A$ denote an offer of restructuring, $M$ subsequent payment
engagement, and $Y$ loss over a fixed horizon. Baseline information $W$ precedes
the offer. A later liquidity assessment $Z$ may be changed by the offer and
affect both engagement and loss. The question therefore requires a declared
intervention on engagement, a target population, an information clock and
assumptions linking the intervention to observed data. R packages supply useful
approaches, but their targets and uncertainty calculations are not interchangeable.
This comparison extends the preceding mediation, medflex, sensemakr and EValue
discussions with CMAverse, medoutcon, regmedint, causalsens, tipr and BayesGmed.
Inspected sources and authored examples support conditional reuse decisions;
they do not establish native qualification. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{A causal target before a software method}

Write $Y_{a,m}$ for the outcome after setting offer and mediator to $(a,m)$,
and $M_a$ for the mediator under offer $a$. Two complementary natural
decompositions on an additive scale are
\[
 \operatorname{TE}=E(Y_{1,M_1}-Y_{0,M_0})
 =\operatorname{PNDE}+\operatorname{TNIE}
 =\operatorname{TNDE}+\operatorname{PNIE}.
\]
Here $\operatorname{PNDE}=E(Y_{1,M_0}-Y_{0,M_0})$ and
$\operatorname{TNIE}=E(Y_{1,M_1}-Y_{1,M_0})$; the other pair interchanges the
reference treatment. The controlled direct effect $E(Y_{1,m}-Y_{0,m})$ instead
holds engagement at the same specified level. It need not equal a natural
effect, and subtracting it from TE need not yield a natural indirect effect.
The selected BayesGmed primary text develops these distinctions under consistency,
positivity, no unmeasured confounding and a cross-world condition. Randomizing
the offer alone does not supply every mediation assumption; a posterior interval
does not establish them either. \citep{exec25_rmed_yimer_paper}

When offer-induced liquidity confounds engagement and loss, an alternative
draws a new mediator $G_b$ from the distribution of $M_b$ conditional on $W$,
independently of the realized intermediate confounder under the declared
intervention law. Let $\mu(a,z,m,w)=E(Y\mid A=a,Z=z,M=m,W=w)$. The selected
D\'iaz and colleagues paper identifies the corresponding mean as
\[
 \theta(a,b)=\int \mu(a,z,m,w)\,p(z\mid a,w)\,
                  p(m\mid b,w)\,p(w)\,d(z,m,w).
\]
The identifying requirements include the relevant treatment and mediator
exchangeabilities, consistency and conditional support. This intervention
differs from drawing a mediator conditional on the intermediate confounder as
well as baseline information. Changing the conditioning set changes the
pathways assigned to direct and indirect components.
\citep{exec25_rmed_diaz_paper}

Define $\operatorname{IDE}=\theta(1,0)-\theta(0,0)$ and
$\operatorname{IIE}=\theta(1,1)-\theta(1,0)$. Their sum is the total contrast
under the randomized mediator intervention, which need not equal the ordinary
treatment effect. An authored example takes
$P(Z=1\mid A=0)=1/4$, $P(Z=1\mid A=1)=1/2$,
$P(M=1\mid Z)=1/4+Z/2$, and $Y=ZM$. The ordinary treatment effect is $3/16$,
whereas IDE is $3/32$ and IIE is $1/16$, summing to $5/32$. All mediator
probabilities are positive. The difference arises from changing dependence in
the intervention, not estimation error. The product must label the two totals
explicitly. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{CMAverse: a broad interface with a consequential draw contract}

CMAverse version 0.1.0 documents regression, weighting, inverse odds weighting,
natural-effect, marginal structural and g-formula approaches. Its interface
restricts methods when post-treatment confounders are supplied and changes
natural-effect labels to randomized analogues. Parameter-function and imputation
estimators have different applicability; the documented logistic and Cox
parameter-function cases require a rare outcome. Its sensitivity interface
distinguishes unmeasured confounding from measurement error and documents a
single-variable measurement-error scope. These are useful capabilities to
compare, provided the proposed product exposes method, scale and restrictions.
\citep{exec25_rmed_cmaverse}

The selected g-formula delegate simulates intermediate confounders from
exposure and baseline covariates, then mediators using those variables and the
simulated intermediate values. In its post-treatment-confounder branch, it
subsequently permutes each mediator column across eligible rows. Outcome
prediction retains the row's baseline and intermediate variables. Global
permutation requires a different justification from a draw conditional on that
row's baseline information; separate column permutations also require
justification when a joint mediator law is intended. \citep{exec25_rmed_cmaverse}

For $W\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)$, mediator probabilities $1/4$ and
$3/4$ in the two baseline groups, and outcome regression $WM$, the
baseline-conditioned stochastic mean is $3/8$. A global shuffle pairs each
row with the marginal mediator probability $1/2$, yielding $1/4$ in expectation.
For two identical balanced binary mediators, $E(M_1M_2)=1/2$; independently
permuting columns yields $1/4$ in expectation. These exact witnesses specify
invariants for an adapter. They are neither native failure frequencies nor a
rejection of g-computation. The route is to declare the conditional joint draw,
reconcile the delegate, and retain an explicitly different target or a separately
reviewed repair. \citep{exec25_rmed_choice}

Conditional R invocation is preferable to porting a large method collection
before resolving its target. Requests should carry mediator order, conditioning
set, treatment contrast, scale, simulation budget and random state. Resampling
units must match the data law: a row bootstrap is not automatically branch-cluster
or shared-calendar inference. Imputation, simulation integration and bootstrap
variation require separate accounting. The GPL declaration and full dependency
inventory also accompany contemplated redistribution; this source review does
not clear every artifact. \citep{exec25_rmed_cmaverse,exec25_rmed_choice}

\subsection{medoutcon: efficient scores and the sampling contract}

medoutcon targets natural and interventional effects using one-step and targeted
minimum loss estimators. The primary paper assumes independent, identically
distributed observations, derives an efficient influence function, and requires
positivity and products of nuisance-estimation errors vanishing faster than
$n^{-1/2}$. Cross-fitting relaxes empirical-process restrictions; it does not
prove those rates for arbitrary learners or remove hidden confounding and
dependence. A low-dimensional intermediate-confounder representation avoids
directly estimating a high-dimensional mediator density, a useful advantage
for multivariate engagement measurements within the stated conditions.
\citep{exec25_rmed_diaz_paper}

The selected source switches to natural effects when $Z$ is explicitly absent,
constructs binary contrasts, and rescales outcomes by their observed range.
A constant outcome makes that scaling denominator zero. Contrasts subtract
influence scores before variance calculation; propensity clipping must be
recorded as a numerical choice rather than proof of population support. For
two-phase mediator measurement, the source uses
\[
 D_{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac{R}{\pi}D
                 -\left(\frac{R}{\pi}-1\right)m_D,
\]
where $R$ indicates observation, $\pi$ is inclusion probability and $m_D$
predicts the complete-data influence quantity. With $D=3$, $m_D=1$ and
$\pi=1/2$, the observed and missing cases give 5 and 1, averaging to 3 under
that law. False inclusion probabilities do not become valid through calculation.
\citep{exec25_rmed_medoutcon,exec25_rmed_choice}

a posterior sample does not establish the restrictions. The useful C++ question

uncertainty, and which apparent reuse would silently change the problem.

\[

\]
This covariance representation can include correlated disturbances; it does not
make a coefficient product causally identified. A proposed adapter should retain

remain explicit inputs.~\citep{exec25_cmed_openmx}

permits it and an inverse computation otherwise. In the dense inverse branch it
forms a full-pivot LU decomposition and solves against the identity. The nearby
sparse branch checks the factorization status, records an iteration error and
sets its inverse buffer to missing values on failure. This is a difference in
the inspected local guards, not evidence that every dense singular model is
accepted by the whole package. Complete fit-function propagation and native

mean, a modified treatment policy or a descriptive path model. This comparison

mediator and outcome regressions and returns the product of the two relevant

conditioning and the scientific assumptions attached to a coefficient product.
The main entry point removes missing observations jointly from the current
variables. In a bank panel, that complete-case set can be a different population
from all eligible customers. Selection and information timing must therefore
be represented outside the regression call.~\citep{exec25_omed_canlab}

and replaces them until its iteration cap is reached. It also reseeds the random
generator from the clock. These are substantive reproducibility and sampling

samples contain two constant samples. Removing them leaves only $(0,1)$ and

mediation coverage rate; it demonstrates why the replacement rule and every
